result.text: 01.Index 02.Projects 03.About Contact ← All projects Category Project (2026 — AI agent platform) AI test users that run your real flows — and a backend built like infrastructure. Walkthru is a launch check for apps built with AI. Persona agents try your real signup, onboarding and checkout flows inside your own browser, think aloud, and report exactly where they got stuck — with the step, the screenshot and the reason. The browser is the hands; the server is the brain. Everything that can be code is code: only the persona session is an agent, and every rule about where it may act is enforced on the server. Live at trywalkthru.com. A deployed browser-agent platform with a Chrome extension, durable job queue and remote MCP server. Python / FastAPI / LangGraph / LangSmith / PostgreSQL / Supabase (RLS) / MCP / Chrome MV3 / TypeScript Live siteGitHub repo API tests (+90 extension tests) MCP tools, per-key rate limited deterministic scanners HTTP call per agent step (Engineering) Engineering highlights LangGraph decide → act → check loop with interrupt()/Command(resume) — one HTTP call per step, state in a Postgres checkpointer, API stateless and horizontally scalable Code safety gate (_enforce) re-checked every step: hallucinated elements, pay/delete actions and unverified-site writes are replaced or safely stopped Durable Postgres job queue — FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, 15-minute leases, per-kind attempt budgets, exponential backoff with jitter Multi-provider LLM chain (Claude Haiku on Vertex → Groq gpt-oss → Gemini) behind a circuit breaker with strict per-provider timeouts SSRF-safe fetcher: resolve once, block private/metadata/IPv4-in-IPv6 ranges, pin the connection, re-validate every redirect Remote MCP server (streamable HTTP) — 24 tools, SHA-256-hashed keys, Postgres-backed per-key limits LangSmith evals on easy/hard/showcase fixture sites full of traps; findings without real evidence are dropped in code (01) Browser on the user's machine, brain on the server. A Chrome MV3 extension (WXT, TypeScript) snapshots the DOM including open shadow roots, masks PII in-page, runs axe-core and Core Web Vitals, and executes actions. FastAPI and LangGraph decide. No headless Chromium on servers, so hosting stays near zero and logged-in pages work without anyone sharing a password. (02) One HTTP call per agent step. (03) Prompts are never a safety boundary. (04) Fail soft, never fake. (05) The scanner can't be turned into an SSRF. (06) Grounded, measured, regression-tested. Hiring for backend, platform or AI engineering? I reply within a day. I've shipped a three-service distributed system with a 20 Hz realtime loop, a WebRTC mesh verified against a live server, hybrid multimodal retrieval with cited answers, and LangGraph agents with checkpointed state, durable Postgres queues, circuit-broken model chains and LangSmith evals. Computer Science (IoT, Cybersecurity & Blockchain) at Heritage Institute of Technology, CGPA 9.02. Smart India Hackathon 2025 national finalist. observation.text: 01.Index 02.Projects 03.About Contact ← All projects Category Project (2026 — AI agent platform) AI test users that run your real flows — and a backend built like infrastructure. Walkthru is a launch check for apps built with AI. Persona agents try your real signup, onboarding and checkout flows inside your own browser, think aloud, and report exactly where they got stuck — with the step, the screenshot and the reason. The browser is the hands; the server is the brain. Everything that can be code is code: only the persona session is an agent, and every rule about where it may act is enforced on the server. Live at trywalkthru.com. A deployed browser-agent platform with a Chrome extension, durable job queue and remote MCP server. Python / FastAPI / LangGraph / LangSmith / PostgreSQL / Supabase (RLS) / MCP / Chrome MV3 / TypeScript Live siteGitHub repo API tests (+90 extension tests) MCP tools, per-key rate limited deterministic scanners HTTP call per agent step (Engineering) Engineering highlights LangGraph decide → act → check loop with interrupt()/Command(resume) — one HTTP call per step, state in a Postgres checkpointer, API stateless and horizontally scalable Code safety gate (_enforce) re-checked every step: hallucinated elements, pay/delete actions and unverified-site writes are replaced or safely stopped Durable Postgres job queue — FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, 15-minute leases, per-kind attempt budgets, exponential backoff with jitter Multi-provider LLM chain (Claude Haiku on Vertex → Groq gpt-oss → Gemini) behind a circuit breaker with strict per-provider timeouts SSRF-safe fetcher: resolve once, block private/metadata/IPv4-in-IPv6 ranges, pin the connection, re-validate every redirect Remote MCP server (streamable HTTP) — 24 tools, SHA-256-hashed keys, Postgres-backed per-key limits LangSmith evals on easy/hard/showcase fixture sites full of traps; findings without real evidence are dropped in code (01) Browser on the user's machine, brain on the server. A Chrome MV3 extension (WXT, TypeScript) snapshots the DOM including open shadow roots, masks PII in-page, runs axe-core and Core Web Vitals, and executes actions. FastAPI and LangGraph decide. No headless Chromium on servers, so hosting stays near zero and logged-in pages work without anyone sharing a password. (02) One HTTP call per agent step. (03) Prompts are never a safety boundary. (04) Fail soft, never fake. (05) The scanner can't be turned into an SSRF. (06) Grounded, measured, regression-tested. (Next project) Agentic planner↗ Let's talk↗ [email] Write a message Résumé ElsewhereGitHub LinkedIn X Hashnode How to reach meFastest way to reach me is email. LinkedIn works too — I check it daily. Hiring for backend, platform or AI engineering? I reply within a day. LocalKolkata, India · 15:25 Open to backend, AI and platform engineering internships and full-time roles — remote or on-site. © 2026 Rohit Maity Theme 02 / 05

observation.text: 01.Index 02.Projects 03.About Contact ← All projects Category Project (2026 — AI agent platform) AI test users that run your real flows — and a backend built like infrastructure. Walkthru is a launch check for apps built with AI. Persona agents try your real signup, onboarding and checkout flows inside your own browser, think aloud, and report exactly where they got stuck — with the step, the screenshot and the reason. The browser is the hands; the server is the brain. Everything that can be code is code: only the persona session is an agent, and every rule about where it may act is enforced on the server. Live at trywalkthru.com. A deployed browser-agent platform with a Chrome extension, durable job queue and remote MCP server. Python / FastAPI / LangGraph / LangSmith / PostgreSQL / Supabase (RLS) / MCP / Chrome MV3 / TypeScript Live siteGitHub repo API tests (+90 extension tests) MCP tools, per-key rate limited deterministic scanners HTTP call per agent step (Engineering) Engineering highlights LangGraph decide → act → check loop with interrupt()/Command(resume) — one HTTP call per step, state in a Postgres checkpointer, API stateless and horizontally scalable Code safety gate (_enforce) re-checked every step: hallucinated elements, pay/delete actions and unverified-site writes are replaced or safely stopped Durable Postgres job queue — FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, 15-minute leases, per-kind attempt budgets, exponential backoff with jitter Multi-provider LLM chain (Claude Haiku on Vertex → Groq gpt-oss → Gemini) behind a circuit breaker with strict per-provider timeouts SSRF-safe fetcher: resolve once, block private/metadata/IPv4-in-IPv6 ranges, pin the connection, re-validate every redirect Remote MCP server (streamable HTTP) — 24 tools, SHA-256-hashed keys, Postgres-backed per-key limits LangSmith evals on easy/hard/showcase fixture sites full of traps; findings without real evidence are dropped in code (01) Browser on the user's machine, brain on the server. A Chrome MV3 extension (WXT, TypeScript) snapshots the DOM including open shadow roots, masks PII in-page, runs axe-core and Core Web Vitals, and executes actions. FastAPI and LangGraph decide. No headless Chromium on servers, so hosting stays near zero and logged-in pages work without anyone sharing a password. (02) One HTTP call per agent step. (03) Prompts are never a safety boundary. (04) Fail soft, never fake. (05) The scanner can't be turned into an SSRF. (06) Grounded, measured, regression-tested. (Next project) Agentic planner↗ Let's talk↗ [email] Write a message Résumé ElsewhereGitHub LinkedIn X Hashnode How to reach meFastest way to reach me is email. LinkedIn works too — I check it daily. Hiring for backend, platform or AI engineering? I reply within a day. LocalKolkata, India · 15:25 Open to backend, AI and platform engineering internships and full-time roles — remote or on-site. © 2026 Rohit Maity Theme 02 / 05

outputs.first_text: 01.Index 02.Projects 03.About Contact (Kolkata, India) A. Backend & AI Engineer Backend engineer first. I design the parts that keep a product standing — service boundaries, queues, caches, rate limits, auth — and I build AI into those systems, not around them. I've shipped a three-service distributed system with a 20 Hz realtime loop, a WebRTC mesh verified against a live server, hybrid multimodal retrieval with cited answers, and LangGraph agents with checkpointed state, durable Postgres queues, circuit-broken model chains and LangSmith evals. Computer Science (IoT, Cybersecurity & Blockchain) at Heritage Institute of Technology, CGPA 9.02. Smart India Hackathon 2025 national finalist. observation.text: 01.Index 02.Projects 03.About Contact ← All projects Category Project (2026 — AI agent platform) AI test users that run your real flows — and a backend built like infrastructure. Walkthru is a launch check for apps built with AI. Persona agents try your real signup, onboarding and checkout flows inside your own browser, think aloud, and report exactly where they got stuck — with the step, the screenshot and the reason. The browser is the hands; the server is the brain. Everything that can be code is code: only the persona session is an agent, and every rule about where it may act is enforced on the server. Live at trywalkthru.com. A deployed browser-agent platform with a Chrome extension, durable job queue and remote MCP server. Python / FastAPI / LangGraph / LangSmith / PostgreSQL / Supabase (RLS) / MCP / Chrome MV3 / TypeScript Live siteGitHub repo API tests (+90 extension tests) MCP tools, per-key rate limited deterministic scanners HTTP call per agent step (Engineering) Engineering highlights LangGraph decide → act → check loop with interrupt()/Command(resume) — one HTTP call per step, state in a Postgres checkpointer, API stateless and horizontally scalable Code safety gate (_enforce) re-checked every step: hallucinated elements, pay/delete actions and unverified-site writes are replaced or safely stopped Durable Postgres job queue — FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, 15-minute leases, per-kind attempt budgets, exponential backoff with jitter Multi-provider LLM chain (Claude Haiku on Vertex → Groq gpt-oss → Gemini) behind a circuit breaker with strict per-provider timeouts SSRF-safe fetcher: resolve once, block private/metadata/IPv4-in-IPv6 ranges, pin the connection, re-validate every redirect Remote MCP server (streamable HTTP) — 24 tools, SHA-256-hashed keys, Postgres-backed per-key limits LangSmith evals on easy/hard/showcase fixture sites full of traps; findings without real evidence are dropped in code (01) Browser on the user's machine, brain on the server. A Chrome MV3 extension (WXT, TypeScript) snapshots the DOM including open shadow roots, masks PII in-page, runs axe-core and Core Web Vitals, and executes actions. FastAPI and LangGraph decide. No headless Chromium on servers, so hosting stays near zero and logged-in pages work without anyone sharing a password. (02) One HTTP call per agent step. (03) Prompts are never a safety boundary. (04) Fail soft, never fake. (05) The scanner can't be turned into an SSRF. (06) Grounded, measured, regression-tested. (Next project) Agentic planner↗ Let's talk↗ [email] Write a message Résumé ElsewhereGitHub LinkedIn X Hashnode How to reach meFastest way to reach me is email. LinkedIn works too — I check it daily. Hiring for backend, platform or AI engineering? I reply within a day. observation.text: 01.Index 02.Projects 03.About Contact ← All projects Category Project (2026 — AI agent platform) AI test users that run your real flows — and a backend built like infrastructure. Walkthru is a launch check for apps built with AI. Persona agents try your real signup, onboarding and checkout flows inside your own browser, think aloud, and report exactly where they got stuck — with the step, the screenshot and the reason. The browser is the hands; the server is the brain. Everything that can be code is code: only the persona session is an agent, and every rule about where it may act is enforced on the server. Live at trywalkthru.com. A deployed browser-agent platform with a Chrome extension, durable job queue and remote MCP server. Python / FastAPI / LangGraph / LangSmith / PostgreSQL / Supabase (RLS) / MCP / Chrome MV3 / TypeScript Live siteGitHub repo API tests (+90 extension tests) MCP tools, per-key rate limited deterministic scanners HTTP call per agent step (Engineering) Engineering highlights LangGraph decide → act → check loop with interrupt()/Command(resume) — one HTTP call per step, state in a Postgres checkpointer, API stateless and horizontally scalable Code safety gate (_enforce) re-checked every step: hallucinated elements, pay/delete actions and unverified-site writes are replaced or safely stopped Durable Postgres job queue — FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, 15-minute leases, per-kind attempt budgets, exponential backoff with jitter Multi-provider LLM chain (Claude Haiku on Vertex → Groq gpt-oss → Gemini) behind a circuit breaker with strict per-provider timeouts SSRF-safe fetcher: resolve once, block private/metadata/IPv4-in-IPv6 ranges, pin the connection, re-validate every redirect Remote MCP server (streamable HTTP) — 24 tools, SHA-256-hashed keys, Postgres-backed per-key limits LangSmith evals on easy/hard/showcase fixture sites full of traps; findings without real evidence are dropped in code (01) Browser on the user's machine, brain on the server. A Chrome MV3 extension (WXT, TypeScript) snapshots the DOM including open shadow roots, masks PII in-page, runs axe-core and Core Web Vitals, and executes actions. FastAPI and LangGraph decide. No headless Chromium on servers, so hosting stays near zero and logged-in pages work without anyone sharing a password. (02) One HTTP call per agent step. (03) Prompts are never a safety boundary. (04) Fail soft, never fake. (05) The scanner can't be turned into an SSRF. (06) Grounded, measured, regression-tested. (Next project) Agentic planner↗ Let's talk↗ [email] Write a message Résumé ElsewhereGitHub LinkedIn X Hashnode How to reach meFastest way to reach me is email. LinkedIn works too — I check it daily. Hiring for backend, platform or AI engineering? I reply within a day. LocalKolkata, India · 15:25 Open to backend, AI and platform engineering internships and full-time roles — remote or on-site. © 2026 Rohit Maity Theme 02 / 05

inputs.first_text: 01.Index 02.Projects 03.About Contact (Kolkata, India) A. Backend & AI Engineer Backend engineer first. I design the parts that keep a product standing — service boundaries, queues, caches, rate limits, auth — and I build AI into those systems, not around them. I've shipped a three-service distributed system with a 20 Hz realtime loop, a WebRTC mesh verified against a live server, hybrid multimodal retrieval with cited answers, and LangGraph agents with checkpointed state, durable Postgres queues, circuit-broken model chains and LangSmith evals. Computer Science (IoT, Cybersecurity & Blockchain) at Heritage Institute of Technology, CGPA 9.02. Smart India Hackathon 2025 national finalist. seo.title: No h1 heading
seo.detail: The page has no top-level heading. Advisory: a clear main heading helps visitors and screen-reader users find the topic; search engines also read prominent headings. Found on 8 of 8 audited pages.
seo.fix: Add one main heading that states what the page is about.

seo.title: No canonical link
seo.detail: Without a canonical URL, variants like ?utm= or trailing slashes can split ranking signals. Found on 8 of 8 audited pages.
seo.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="..."> pointing at the preferred URL.

seo.title: Page title is too short
seo.detail: The title is "Rohit Maity" (11 characters). Advisory: a very short title may say little about the page. Found on 7 of 8 audited pages.
seo.fix: Describe this page and the brand in the title. There is no required length.

seo.title: Missing meta description
seo.detail: No meta description. Advisory: search engines usually build snippets from page text, and link previews often show the description when it exists. Found on 7 of 8 audited pages.
seo.fix: Add a short description of what this page offers and for whom. There is no required length.

seo.title: No sitemap.xml
seo.detail: Search engines discover pages slower without a sitemap.
seo.fix: Generate /sitemap.xml and reference it from robots.txt.

seo.title: Duplicate title
seo.detail: Several pages share the same title, so search engines cannot tell them apart and may show only one. Found on 7 of 8 audited pages.
seo.fix: Give each page its own title; for true duplicates, pick one URL and point the others at it with rel=canonical or a redirect.

geo.title: The homepage says little before JavaScript runs
geo.detail: AI crawlers read 18 words on your homepage. That is thin for an assistant to explain what you do and for whom.
geo.fix: Put a plain two or three sentence description of the product, who it is for and what it costs in the server-rendered HTML.

geo.title: No structured data

geo.title: Few section headings
geo.detail: Pages with fewer than two h2 headings are harder for assistants to split into quotable answers.
geo.fix: Break each page into sections with descriptive h2 headings (for example 'How it works', 'Pricing', 'Who it is for').

geo.title: No plain answer near the top

geo.fix: Link to an about page and a contact page from the homepage header or footer.
